blocks.passage:
Running an import or export operation means turning a single deal into a repeatable process. You have dozens of shipments in motion — some leaving the factory, some at sea, some clearing customs, some being invoiced. Each one has a story, and each one needs attention at a different moment.

The people who do this well share one habit: they separate the routine from the exception. Ninety per cent of shipments follow a standard path. They deserve a standard process, not endless emails. The remaining ten per cent, the exceptions, deserve real thinking.

A good trade operator spends most of the day protecting the exceptions from interrupting the routine, and most of the week making sure the routine actually holds.

items.q: What does running an operation mean, according to the text?
options: Turning a single deal into a repeatable process
items.why: "Running an import or export operation means turning a single deal into a repeatable process."

items.q: What habit do the best trade operators share?
options: Separating the routine from the exception
items.why: "they separate the routine from the exception."

items.q: What proportion of shipments follow a standard path?
items.why: "Ninety per cent of shipments follow a standard path."

items.q: Why should routine shipments get a standard process, not endless emails?
options: So attention is saved for the exceptions that need real thinking
items.why: Inferência: padronizar o rotineiro libera atenção para os 10% de exceções.

items.q: What does a good trade operator spend most of the week doing?
options: Making sure the routine actually holds
items.why: "most of the week making sure the routine actually holds."

audio.text:
Right, Monday review. We've got forty live shipments on the board, so let's not go through all of them one by one — that would take the whole morning.

Here's how I want to run this. Most of these are routine: they're moving as planned, the documents are in order, nothing needed. I'm going to mark those green and move on fast. If it's on track, we don't discuss it.

What I want to spend our time on is the exceptions. Right now I count four. One container is stuck in customs in Rotterdam. One shipment is at risk because the vessel was delayed. One invoice is disputed by the customer. And one supplier has flagged a possible delay next week.

Those four get real attention today. For each, I want to know: what's the problem, what are our options, and who owns the next step.

The routine protects itself if the process is good. Our job this morning is to stop those four exceptions from quietly turning into ten.

items.q: How many live shipments are on the board?
items.why: "We've got forty live shipments on the board."

items.q: How does James handle the routine shipments?
options: Marks them green and moves on fast
items.why: "I'm going to mark those green and move on fast. If it's on track, we don't discuss it."

items.q: How many exceptions does James count?
items.why: "Right now I count four."

items.q: For each exception, what three things does James want to know?
options: The customer, the price and the date
The problem, the options, and who owns the next step
The vessel, the port and the invoice
items.why: "what's the problem, what are our options, and who owns the next step."

items.q: What is the goal of the morning, in James's words?
options: To stop four exceptions from quietly turning into ten
items.why: "stop those four exceptions from quietly turning into ten."

items.q: "The shipment is **in transit**." In transit means…
items.why: In transit = em trânsito.

items.q: "That's an **exception**, not routine." An exception is…
options: a case that falls outside the normal path
items.why: Exception = exceção, caso fora do padrão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We need to **___** this shipment — the customer needs it urgently."
items.why: To expedite = acelerar, agilizar.

items.q: A **backlog** is…
options: work that has piled up and is overdue
items.why: Backlog = atraso acumulado, fila de pendências.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "There are ten deals in the **___** for next month."
items.why: Pipeline = fluxo do que está por vir.

items.q: "Let's **keep an eye on** the delayed vessel." To keep an eye on means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = ficar de olho, monitorar.

items.q: "That customs issue could **hold up** the whole order." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, travar.

items.q: "Can you **chase up** the missing documents?" To chase up means to…
options: follow up to get something done
items.why: Chase up = cobrar/perseguir uma pendência.

items.q: "Three orders are **piling up** at the port." To pile up means to…
items.why: Pile up = acumular-se.

items.q: "Let's **stay on top of** the exceptions this week." To stay on top of means to…
items.why: Stay on top of = manter sob controle.
